subject: Risk & Compliance
title: Dual-Class Share Structures
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Dual-Class Share Structures.

hook.text: Mark Zuckerberg owns 13% of Meta but controls 58% of the votes. Your shares count less than his.

buildup.text: Dual-class structures give founders super-voting shares, maintaining control even as they sell equity.

discovery.text: Google, Meta, and Snap all went public with dual-class shares. Founders kept control regardless of ownership.

twist.text: Index providers like S&P have started excluding dual-class companies. Investors are pushing back.

climax.text: Dual-class shares protect founders' vision but violate one-share-one-vote democracy. The tension is unresolved.

punchline.text: 13% ownership. 58% control. Not all shares are equal.

quiz.question: What do dual-class shares allow founders to do?
options: Maintain voting control with a minority ownership stake
